# AI system records

> A mapping aid for engineers, architects and auditors. It records which controls have checked evidence in which repository and where there are gaps. It is not legal advice, not a conformity assessment and not a statement that any system complies with anything.

## Customer-support agent (reference system)

A back-end agent that answers customer-support questions from a knowledge base and can propose state-changing actions such as a refund, which a person must approve. It is assembled from the repositories listed below. It is a reference design, not a deployed product.

| | |
|---|---|
| Intended purpose | Assist support staff and customers by answering questions from approved documents and preparing actions for human approval. |
| Provider role | The repository owner builds and publishes the reference components; whoever deploys them becomes the provider of the resulting system for the purposes of the AI Act and must make that determination. |
| Deployer role | Not applicable to the reference repositories; applies to the organisation that runs a deployment. |
| Risk classification | Not classified. Customer support is not obviously an Annex III use, but classification depends on the actual purpose and context and is a legal judgement that this pack does not make. Article 50 transparency duties would apply to a customer-facing chat. |
| Human oversight | Every state-changing action needs approval. The approval service binds approvals to exact arguments, makes them single use, separates requester and approver, and supports quorum and veto. Read-only actions are auto-approved by policy. |
| Logging | Hash-chained audit logs in the agent harness, the approval service and the gateway; content fingerprinted and redacted by default; traces carry no message content by default. |
| Data | Knowledge-base articles and order and customer records reached through governed tools. Personal data is masked by default in the lakehouse and in logs. No model training or fine-tuning is done. |

### Components

| Repository | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [claude-agent-reference](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/claude-agent-reference) | Agent loop with budgets, approval-gated tools and an audit log. |
| [agent-guardrails-gateway](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/agent-guardrails-gateway) | Policy enforcement at the tool boundary with signed grants and taint tracking. |
| [human-in-the-loop-inbox](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/human-in-the-loop-inbox) | Approval workflow for actions that need a person. |
| [agent-eval-harness](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/agent-eval-harness) | Regression gate for changes to the agent. |
| [agent-tracing-otel](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/agent-tracing-otel) | Traces and cost per completed task, content off by default. |
| [governed-data-agents](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/governed-data-agents) | Governed natural-language access to analytical data. |
| [databricks-medallion-lakehouse](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/databricks-medallion-lakehouse) | Governed lakehouse that holds the analytical data. |
| [azure-ai-landing-zone](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/azure-ai-landing-zone) | Private, keyless infrastructure for model endpoints. |
| [ai-platform-reference-architecture](https://github.com/darshansatpathy/ai-platform-reference-architecture) | The architecture, risk register and operating model the other components sit in. |

### Known limitations

- Reference design: no deployment, no users and no production traffic have been observed.
- No disclosure to end users that they are talking to an AI system (see EUAIA-50).
- No declared accuracy level; the evaluation set covers an invented product.
- Human oversight quality depends on approvers who are not modelled here.
- Risk classification, impact assessment and data protection assessment have not been done.
